parsed.main_gap: The constructive half of the Refinement Lemma (Xiang achieving D ≤ Γ with ≤ q−1 cuts) is only sketched: the overlay pairing and the crucial cut-count |A|+|B|−1+(q−|A|−|B|)=q−1 are asserted, 'details omitted'.

errors.description: Upper-bound half of the refinement lemma: the overlay/common-refinement construction and, critically, the claim that it uses at most q−1 cuts are stated without proof. This step is essential for the upper bound c ≤ 2^n/(2^{n+1}−1); it is verifiable and tight, but as written it is an unproved assertion.
errors.quote: and use at most \(q-1\) cuts in total (standard; details omitted).

errors.description: The 56-unit 'grid example' is presented as agreeing with the theorem, but Liu's intervals (7,14,35) have Γ=7/56=1/8, so optimal Xiang play holds Liu to 9/16 < 4/7; the displayed Xiang moves (8,38) are simply suboptimal. The claimed 'agreement' is misleading (though only offered as evidence, not proof).
errors.quote:
Sorting gives Liu
\((18+13+1)/56=32/56=4/7\), in agreement with the theorem.

errors.description: Minor: in the lower-bound graph argument, the exclusion of loops from the chosen tree component (needed since a loop edge would contribute ±(x_{2j-1}+x_{2j}) rather than ±(x_{2j-1}−x_{2j})) is not spelled out, although it follows from e_C=v_C−1 with connectivity.
errors.quote: Loops and parallel edges are allowed.

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}−1) and the main structure (greedy drafting value (1+D)/2; D_min = minimal subset-sum gap; pigeonhole; binary construction) are correct, and the graph-theoretic lower-bound half is fully rigorous. Only the constructive half is left unproved.
